issues.legal_issue: A family arrangement that only records steps for dividing property in the future, without itself creating rights in specific immovable property, does not require registration.
material_facts: The document described as an award recorded a family arrangement and proposed steps for dividing the family properties in the future.
It did not allot specific items of immovable property or itself create rights in particular properties.
A prior court had held the document inadmissible because it was not registered.
issues.conclusion: The document was a memorandum of understanding or family arrangement that did not require registration; the prior order holding it inadmissible for want of registration was incorrect.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17(1)(b) and 17(2)(v) of the Registration Act, 1908, a document that does not itself create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish rights in specific immovable property, but merely creates a right to obtain a later document that will do so, is exempt from compulsory registration. The court applied Ranjangam Iyer v. Ranjangam Iyer and distinguished documents that themselves allot specific property, as discussed in Shiromani v. Hem Kumar, Satish Kumar v. Surinder Kumar, and Lachhman Dass v. Ram Lal. It also considered the family-arrangement principles in Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation.

predicates.family_partition_document_dispute: The dispute concerns a document recording an arrangement to divide family property.
predicates.document_only_records_future_division: The document records steps or an arrangement for dividing the property in the future rather than effecting the division itself.
predicates.document_creates_rights_in_specific_prop: The document itself creates, declares, assigns, limits or extinguishes a person's rights in a specific item of immovable property.

issues.definition: When a document in a family-property division dispute only records a future division and does not itself create rights in specific property, the document is exempt from registration.

issues.legal_issue: A final, unchallenged finding that family properties were partitioned bars a later suit seeking partition and separate possession of those same properties.
material_facts: In an earlier appeal concerning the family properties, the court found that the properties had been partitioned among the family members.
No party challenged that finding, and it attained finality; the partition had also been acted upon.
A later suit sought partition and separate possession of the same properties.
The plaintiff argued that the earlier finding exceeded the scope of a remand, but had not challenged that finding in the earlier proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The earlier finding of partition was binding, the principle of res judicata applied, and the later suit for partition and separate possession was not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure embodies the principle of res judicata. A matter of fact, or a mixed question of law and fact, decided between the parties in an earlier proceeding cannot be reopened in later litigation. An erroneous decision may still operate as res judicata; an exception may apply to a pure question of law concerning jurisdiction or a decision sanctioning something illegal. The court relied on Mathura Prasad Sarjoo Jaiswal v. Dossibai N.B. Jeejeebhoy, Mohanlal Goenka v. Benoy Kishna Mukherjee, and State of West Bengal v. Hemant Kumar Bhattacharjee, and distinguished Asrar Ahmed v. Durgah Committee.

rule.if: later_partition_suit and prior_adjudication_concerned_same_properties and prior_finding_was_that_partition_occurred and prior_finding_was_not_challenged and prior_finding_became_final and prior_partition_was_acted_on

predicates.later_partition_suit: A party brings a later suit seeking partition and separate possession of family properties.
predicates.prior_adjudication_concerned_same_proper: An earlier proceeding adjudicated a matter concerning the same properties.
predicates.prior_finding_was_that_partition_occurre: The earlier court found that the properties had already been partitioned.
predicates.prior_finding_was_not_challenged: The party bound by the earlier finding did not challenge it in the available proceedings.
predicates.prior_partition_was_acted_on: The family members acted upon the partition found to have occurred.

issues.definition: A later suit for partition and separate possession is barred when an earlier final, unchallenged finding concerning the same properties established a partition that was acted upon.
